title: k6 is not installed, so the load suite cannot run at all
body:
WHAT IS MISSING
The k6 binary is not installed on this machine. `npm run test:load` maps to
`k6 run tests/load/baseline.js`, so the load lane's entire suite cannot execute
-- not "fails", cannot start.

REPRODUCTION
  $ k6 version
  bash: k6: command not found
  $ where.exe k6
  INFO: Could not find files for the given pattern(s).

VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED
Absence confirmed by PATH lookup plus a direct check of the usual install
locations: Program Files\k6, Program Files (x86)\k6, ProgramData\chocolatey\bin,
scoop apps, and the WinGet Links shim directory. None exist.

WHO CAN CLEAR IT
A person, because this installs software. Both installers are present on the
machine (verified by `command -v`):
  winget install k6.k6        (winget: available)
  choco install k6            (chocolatey: available)
A new shell is needed afterwards for PATH to pick it up.

NOT BLOCKED ON THIS
BASE_URL is not a second blocker. The app under test is present at a sibling
checkout with node_modules and a .next build already in place, so the load lane
can start its own target with `next start` for the duration of a run and does
not need an environment published to it. If a shared staging target is wanted
instead, that is a separate decision and I will raise it separately.

title: baseline k6 run against a local production build of the app under test
body:
tests/load/baseline.js is a 2-minute ramp (30s to 10 VUs, 1m hold, 30s down) over /, /plan and /results, with thresholds on http_req_failed and per-route http_req_duration.

STATE: cannot execute -- see the referenced blocker.

WHAT I CONFIRMED WITHOUT k6
All three routes the script targets exist in the app under test: app/page.tsx,
app/plan/page.tsx, app/results/page.tsx. Read from the source tree, NOT executed
-- I have not yet served the app or issued a single HTTP request against it.

WHAT I HAVE NOT DONE
No run, no measurement, no numbers. The thresholds in the script
(static p95<300/p99<800, results p95<800/p99<2000) are as-authored guesses and
have never been checked against an observed distribution. Treat them as
unvalidated until a first run exists.
